answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent identities to a cryptographic stake burning curve where cost scales superlinearly: minting the nth identity requires burning O(n^2) tokens. An attacker amassing identities faces quadratic financial friction, destroying economic viability. Stake commitment records are sealed into an immutable onyx ledger, verifiable by peers. Legitimate participants deposit modest collateral into a hard walnut vault, harvesting protocol nectar through verifiable utility while fraudulent clustering collapses.
